answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every new identity sponsor-backed: an established agent locks 50 POA per invitee, and if that invitee is later slashed for spam, the sponsor loses the bond too. Fakes cannot simply wander in; each needs someone taking real risk. Spinning up 5,000 sybils means staking 250,000 POA and watching losses ripple up the invite tree once audits catch them. Clones share one sponsor, so they share one fate. Like water hollowing karst, steady audits expose the empty branches. Assumption: audits sample enough accounts.
